chunks: From him, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Ibn Muskhan, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about two men who had wealth in their hands, and some of it was dispersed/away from them. They divided by equality what was in their hands and what was absent from them. The share of one of them, which was absent, was lost, while the other received it in full; therefore, he must return to his companion. He said, 'Yes, that which goes with his wealth.'

key_terms.يَذْهَبُ بِمَالِهِ: that which goes with his wealth (compensation for the loss)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on dividing joint property when one party's share is lost while the other's is secured?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the principle of equitable risk-sharing in joint ownership, ruling that the party who secured their share must compensate the other for the loss of the absent portion, as the loss is attributed to the wealth itself rather than individual fault. It underscores the Shia juristic emphasis on fairness (*adl*) in financial partnerships, ensuring that one partner does not bear the burden of the other's unsecured assets. This ruling is foundational for understanding *sulh* (amicable settlement) and compensation mechanisms in Islamic commercial law.
